impact: publishReceipts stages receipt.json and capture-inputs.json, then renames both and fsyncs the evidence directory. Staging is now separated from committing, so a failure during staging leaves both destinations untouched, and the directory flush makes each rename durable. What remains is the window BETWEEN the two renames: a crash there leaves the new receipt.json beside the previous capture-inputs.json, a pair that describes two different runs. No raw capture is deleted in that window — deletion happens only after both renames and the read-back — so this cannot destroy evidence; it can leave a committed evidence set internally inconsistent until the next run republishes both. Closing it properly means publishing a generation directory and switching a single pointer (one rename), rather than renaming two files in sequence. That is a change to how evidence is laid out on disk, not a patch to this function, which is why it is filed rather than half-done.
title: T-009: receipt publication is two renames, not one atomic switch
